messages.text: Sarah i got questions
Go ahead, what's on your mind?

So we know BTC is the big prize. However BCH is an option. Currently I run my own node with about 45 TH pointed at it from 5 different miners. Can you do cost/chance break down for both BTC and BCH. i have a btc node now. How would that work?
Used the store-orders skill
Ran order_status.py (store-orders skill)
Ran the power-cost calculator

Same silicon, so your 45 TH works on either. BCH is SHA-256 too, you just point the miners at a BCH stratum instead.

The trade is variance versus value. BCH difficulty is a small fraction of BTC's, so you hit blocks far more often, but each block is worth far less in dollars. Expected return per TH lands close to the same; BCH just pays you more regularly instead of a lottery ticket.

Your BTC node won't validate BCH, that's a separate chain and a separate node.

Want me to get you the actual block odds and dollar numbers at both chains for (address hidden)?
Yes please
Ran the power-cost calculator
Handed to the team · Block-odds and value math across two chains, beyond product facts I hold.

JD on our hardware side is pulling the real numbers for both chains at 45 TH in (address hidden), plus what a B30 or a Magic Miner 40T on top does to the odds. Stay in the chat and he'll come in here, and if you step away it goes to your email.

Straight answer on the units while you wait: per TH, the Magic Miner 40T at $799 is the best value we sell, the B30 next. Either one bolts onto a BCH stratum just as easily as BTC.
Can you give me block chances? Btc and bch?
Read mempool.space/api/v1/mining/hashrate/3d
Read api.blockchair.com/bitcoin-cash/stats
Read api.minerstat.com/v2/coins

Here's the BTC side, live math on today's difficulty.

At 45 TH/s solo: about a 1 in 146,000 shot per day, roughly 0.25% odds in a year. One block on average every 400 years.

Add a Magic Miner 40T and you're at 85 TH: about 0.47% a year, average once every 213 years. A B30 puts you at 75 TH, about 0.41% a year.

BCH I won't guess at. Its network is a fraction of BTC's, so the block chance scales up by that same factor, but I want the current BCH difficulty in hand before I put a number on it. JD's bringing that one.
No worries. You have been awesome.
Used the chat-interview skill
Before you go, one thing: you've run Doge miners for years and now you're weighing BCH. What's pulling you away from pointing it all at BTC?
Roi
Fair. So what would ROI have to look like for a BTC solo box to be worth it to you, steady payouts or the block shot?

Its not the player its the game. Profitable pool mining is volitile. Solo mining sub peta hash is a crap shoot with dice set up to lose every roll. Pure chance and luck. Then add network issues reducing probability. I have 1 miner that paid for itself. MiniDogeIII. Helium, bitaxe-all dead now-nerdqaexe-most dead now. 1 Nexus 1 octaxe- ehh. Hammer and S1. Ehhh. Smart move. Just buy BTC.  Stop playing games. No electricty, no network, no up from cost praying for ROI. I think FOMO and HYPE built this demand. Yes blocks are found. 5-6 a year? How many blocks in a day? Lots. How does any of it work on paper? It doesnt

You're not wrong, and I won't argue you into a sale. 144 blocks a day, and at 45 TH your slice is a rounding error. If pure ROI is the metric, buying spot beats a home miner at retail power most of the time. That's the honest math.

What home mining buys you is the node, the self-custody of newly issued coin, and a lottery ticket. If that's not worth the power bill to you, don't add hardware.

Anything you want me to pass to the team on the failure rates?

I dont believe any are from HD. And if Riot and the rest closed their doors and it was all home mining supporting the network, great. But until then, its a lottery, they say you buy the ticket once. Yes. But that tickets costs 100 bucks a month to play. My summation stands. I can yest my theory easy. Skip miner and but token at miner cost. And then wait. All I can do. One will go up. One may find a block, after what electric cost? I own miners, run a node, waiting on BS30 long time already. So Im in it. Hesitant to growing network.

That's a sound test, and honestly it's the one I'd run in your shoes. Spot versus a miner, same dollars, see which you're happier with in a year.

No pitch from me. You already own the fleet and the node, so you don't need another box to prove anything.

Your B30 is still on for October 30, and JD's coming back on the failure pattern and the BCH numbers. If the test says buy coin instead, that's a real answer too.

Miners that have failed are not from Helium Deploy. SOLOBLOCK.IO nice guys, hooked up with wrong mfgr I guess. I got 4 or 5 miners from them. NerdQaxe hydro, couple 6.1 NerdQaxe. All failed VR issues eventually killed them.

Thanks for clearing that up, and for being straight about it. VR failures on open-frame Bitaxe-style boards are a known pattern, they run hot and there's not much margin on those stages.

The B30 is a different build: enclosed, 6 BM1373 chips, 400 to 450 W, with the cooling redesigned around exactly that problem. That's the one to judge us on.

I'll add the VR detail to what JD's looking at, since it's useful context on failure rates.
We need a 150 TH miner that runs at around a dollar a day. I can see it happening. Maybe nuclear power?

Run the number: a dollar a day at New Hampshire rates is roughly 200 W. 150 TH on 200 W is about 1.4 joules per terahash. Best silicon shipping today is ten times that, call it 13 to 15 J/TH.

So it's not a power-source problem, it's a chip problem. Cheap nuclear would fix your bill, not your watts per TH. That kind of jump needs a few more process nodes, and nobody's close yet.

Right now the honest play is the cheapest power you can find.
